title: Convert unknown input to UTC POSIXct
description:
Since it seems to be the only base conversion method that doesn't screw up the clock time. Otherwise we need to use vctrs, but I don't want to pull it in unless we have to

I think going to UTC is fine, because we handle POSIXct / POSIXlt separately already. Most other classes don't hold onto the time zone in any way

This will allow us to use `slide_period(x, .i = ymon())`

```r
library(zoo)
library(tsibble)
library(datea)
library(dint)

x <- as.Date("1970-01-01")

x_yearmon <- as.yearmon(x)
x_yearmonth <- yearmonth(x)
x_ymon <- as_ymon(x)
x_date_ym <- as_date_ym(x)

as.POSIXct(x_yearmon, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1969-12-31 19:00:00 EST"
as.POSIXct(x_yearmonth, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1969-12-31 19:00:00 EST"
as.POSIXct(x_ymon, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1970-01-01 UTC"
as.POSIXct(x_date_ym, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1969-12-31 19:00:00 EST"

as.POSIXlt(x_yearmon, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1970-01-01 UTC"
as.POSIXlt(x_yearmonth, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1970-01-01 UTC"
as.POSIXlt(x_ymon, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1970-01-01 UTC"
as.POSIXlt(x_date_ym, tz = "UTC")
#> [1] "1970-01-01 UTC"
```

title: ISO week conversion
description:
Easiest to go to `year, week[1, 53], weekday[0, 6]` from `year, ymonth, yday`

http://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html#Example:%20Converting%20between%20the%20civil%20calendar%20and%20the%20ISO%20week%20calendar

Part of #25 ?

```r
warp_year_ymonth_yday(year, ymonth, yday, to = "iso-week")
warp_year_yday(year, yday, to = "iso-week")
warp_month_mday(month, mday, to = "iso-week")
warp_days(days, to = "iso-week")

warp_iso_week(
  year, 
  yweek, 
  wday, 
  to = c("year_ymonth_yday", "year_yday", "month_mday", "days")
)
```

title: warp_wday_from_days()
description:
http://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html#weekday_from_days

```c
(z >= -4 ? (z+4) % 7 : (z+5) % 7 + 6)
```

title: Expose low level converters
description:
No recycling, for speed, but check the sizes and errors accordingly.

Use a macro to support both integers and doubles when there is just one input, especially for `warp_days()` which will often get Date input, which is often a double internally. Should just need: `CTYPE, DEREF, NA_CHECK`, and we will always do `elt = (int) p_x[i]`. `NA_CHECK` will be `elt = NA_INTEGER` or `!R_FINITE (elt)`.

When there are multiple inputs, coerce the vectors to integer unconditionally.

Terminology:
- years = number of years since 1970-01-01
- months = number of months since 1970-01-01
- days = number of days since 1970-01-01
- ymonth = month within the year
- mday = day within the month
- yday = day within the year

---

- `warp_years_ymonth_mday_to_years_yday()` (civil to yy)
- `warp_years_ymonth_mday_to_months_mday()` (civil to mm)
- `warp_years_ymonth_mday_to_days()` (civil to ordinal)

```r
warp_years_ymonth_mday(
  years,
  ymonth,
  mday,
  to = c("years_yday", "months_mday", "days")
)
```

---

- `warp_years_yday_to_years_ymonth_mday()` (yy to civil)
- `warp_years_yday_to_months_mday()` (yy to mm)
- `warp_years_yday_to_days()` (yy to ordinal)

```r
warp_years_yday(
  years,
  yday,
  to = c("years_ymonth_mday", "months_mday", "days")
)
```

---

- `warp_months_mday_to_years_ymonth_mday()` (mm to civil)
- `warp_months_mday_to_years_yday()` (mm to yy)
- `warp_months_mday_to_days()` (mm to ordinal)

```r
warp_months_mday(
  months,
  mday,
  to = c("years_ymonth_mday", "years_yday", "days")
)
```

---

- `warp_days_to_years_ymonth_mday()` (ordinal to civil)
- `warp_days_to_years_yday()` (ordinal to yy)
- `warp_days_to_months_mday()` (ordinal to mm)

```r
warp_days(
  days,
  to = c("years_ymonth_mday", "years_yday", "months_mday")
)
```

---

A few extra that are encapsulated in the above conversions, but might be useful when you don't have information about the exact day, or know that it always starts on the first of the year/month.

- `warp_years_to_months()` (`warp_years_yday_to_months_mday(yday = 0)`)
- `warp_years_to_days()` (`warp_years_yday_to_days(yday = 0)`)

```r
warp_years(
  years,
  to = c("months", "days")
)
```

- `warp_months_to_years_ymonth()` (`warp_months_mday_to_years_ymonth_mday(mday=0)`)
- `warp_months_to_years_yday()` (`warp_months_mday_to_years_yday(mday = 0)`) 
- `warp_months_to_days()` (`warp_months_mday_to_days(mday = 0)`)

```r
warp_months(
  months,
  to = c("years_ymonth", "years_yday", "days")
)
```

---

Then datea could use `warp_months(months, to = "days")` and `warp_months(months, to = "years_ymonth")` and wouldn't need any C code

title: Expose low level utilities
description:
- `warp_floor_divide(x, y)` - internal divmod, returns a list of quotient and remainder
- `warp_floor_divide_quotient(x, y)` - internal divmod, returns integer vector of just quotient
- `warp_floor_divide_remainder(x, y)` - internal divmod, returns integer vector of just remainder
- `warp_floor_divide_quotient2(x, y)` - assumes divisor is positive, faster impl

`warp_floor_divide_quotient2()` would assume the divisor is positive and can take a faster implementation of `(x < 0) ? (x - (y - 1)) / y : x / y` for the quotient. It would only return the quotient.

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4102423/efficiently-implementing-floored-euclidean-integer-division

title: Extend `warp_change()`
description:
```
warp_change(x, ..., period, every, origin, at = c("stops", "starts"), end = FALSE)
```

add dots for future extensibility - can mock `check_dots_empty()` fairly easily without importing ellipsis

No changes to `warp_boundary()` required because they wouldn't make sense. `at = "stops", end = TRUE` would ensure that `1L` is returned. `at = "starts"` would return the change "starts", always including the first value. And with `end = TRUE` it would ensure that the last value is present too

title: Problems with DST and hour and below
description:
These should be in the same group

``` r
x <- as.POSIXct(
  c("1972-01-01 00:00:00", "1972-01-01 01:00:00"),
  "Australia/Melbourne"
)

warp::warp_distance(x, "hour", 6)
#> [1] 2919 2920
```

<sup>Created on 2020-01-08 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9000)</sup>

title: Consider a default for `warp_distance()` of calling `as.POSIXct()` on the input
description:
If we have a `ym` class that doesn't inherit from `"Date"` then we'd need to coerce to a date time class to make it work with `warp_distance()`

Or maybe `vec_cast(x, new_datetime())`?

title: Different distance algorithm
description:
Maybe one that computes everything like it currently does for week. So it would compute the number of months from 1970-01-01, resetting the counter every Jan 1. This would generate different groups for say, every 5 months, because of the reset.

It wouldn’t affect year at all

Then the week algorithm would go here

title: Add tests for half hour DST offsets
Consider always using TZ of x
description:
~So we remove the origin parameter and always use either 1970-01-01 or 0001-01-01 in the time zone of x~ We need the origin still

Construct with `as.POSIXct(“0001-01-01”, tz =)`?

This would mean that if you ever wanted to use those values as offsets then you’d have to know the original time zone, but that seems ok

This would make it less of a hassle because you don’t get the annoying origin warning, and it would automatically do the thing you generally would have done anyways

title: Should `by` just be `period`?
description: I think it would make the docs more straightforward

title: Generalize docs
description: Make by/every/origin more generalized and expand on each. `origin` should mention its default in the description for inheritParams purposes

title: Swap out for new `by = "week"` implementation
description:
That way we support both, since just `by = day, every = 7 * every` is what we did before.

The new way feels more natural and aligns with `lubridate::week()`

title: by = "day" needs to account for DST
description:
I don't think it is as simple as using the seconds, because we have to account for DST. This is wrong

```r
as.POSIXct("2019-03-10 01:59:59", "America/New_York") + c(0:1, 75601, 75600)
#> [1] "2019-03-10 01:59:59 EST" "2019-03-10 03:00:00 EDT"
#> [3] "2019-03-11 00:00:00 EDT" "2019-03-10 23:59:59 EDT"

warp::warp_distance(as.POSIXct("2019-03-10 01:59:59", "America/New_York") + c(0:1, 75601, 75600), "day")
#> Warning: `x` (America/New_York) and `origin` (UTC) do not have the same time
#> zone. Converting `x` to the time zone of `origin`. It is highly advised to
#> provide `x` and `origin` with the same time zone.
#> [1] 17965 17965 17966 17966
```
